user_problem: Countertop microwave ovens develop hot spots that burn food edges while centers stay cold. The household wants even heating without stirring mid-cycle.

mechanism_state.mechanism: A non-contact temperature sensor detects the temperature of each area of the heating chamber, enabling per-zone monitoring that can be used to modulate microwave and radiant heat inputs so hot spots are reduced and cold centers are brought up to temperature.
mechanism_state.intervention: Add an infrared (non-contact) temperature sensor array to the microwave cavity that maps surface temperature across the food in real time, and couple it to a control loop that reduces microwave power (or activates radiant/convective heating) in zones detected as overheating while continuing to heat zones detected as cold, using a mode-stirrer or turntable to redistribute energyâall without user intervention.
mechanism_state.expected_effect: Hot spots at food edges stop burning while cold centers reach target temperature, producing substantially more uniform heating within a single automatic cycle.
